status: proposed authored questions; require Mark/Tram review

questions.question: Beyond principal and interest, which two costs would you include when comparing renting and buying? How is a down payment different from a fee?
questions.hint: Separate costs paid once, costs paid repeatedly, and cash that becomes an asset.

questions.question: Two homes have the same loan payment, but one needs more maintenance and has higher property taxes. Is the monthly housing cost the same? Explain.
questions.hint: Consider what leaves the household budget outside the loan payment.

questions.question: For the same principal and interest rate, how would a 15-year loan differ from a 30-year loan in monthly payment and interest over the entire loan?
questions.hint: Think about the time available to repay the principal.

questions.question: A fictional buyer chooses the lower monthly payment to preserve cash. What possible trade-off should they acknowledge over the full loan term?
questions.hint: A lower monthly commitment and a lower total financing cost are different claims.

questions.question: How might expecting to move in two years instead of seven change the housing decision? Name one assumption or liquidity need that matters.
questions.hint: Look at transaction costs and money available for other needs.

questions.question: Your preferred option has the higher ending value in this model. What would you still need to consider before calling it preferable for the fictional learner?
questions.hint: The model is not the whole situation.

questions.question: What changes when an allocation moves from one company to several different businesses? Does that prevent every loss?
questions.hint: Distinguish one-company risk from risks that affect many investments.

questions.question: All the investment buckets fell in the second fictional round. Does that prove spreading exposure was useless? Explain.
questions.hint: Risk reduction is different from a guarantee.

questions.question: For a fictional goal that needs money soon, how would the time horizon and willingness or ability to absorb a decline affect your allocation?
questions.hint: Relate the choice to when the money is needed.

questions.question: The fictional learner now has a much longer horizon but still dislikes large declines. What changed, and what did not?
questions.hint: The timeline and the tolerance for loss are separate considerations.

questions.question: An allocation earned the most money in this one fictional run. Is that enough to call it the best original decision? Why?
questions.hint: Distinguish what was knowable when choosing from what happened later.

questions.question: A thoughtful allocation lost value. What evidence would help judge the reasoning instead of judging only the result?
questions.hint: Consider the goal, constraints, downside, and information available before the outcome.
